items.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025
items.q: I already knew Mel Lewis where I got to know them pretty quickly by getting back to L.A., and Shelly Manne. And they became like my mentors.

ctx.x: Did that occurrence affect your education or your choice to start working? Or what did it do to the family?

It affected everything because my dad proved that you can take it with you, because he left us not penniless but in dire straits. My mom really had to struggle to get back on her feet so we left where we were living — we lived in Palm Springs, California. And we left there and went back to Los Angeles where we had been up until when I started high school. I got to L.A. and just immediately got on the scene there. I didn’t finish my last semester of high school and ended up dropping out before graduation. But I…

Was there an audition piece — I remember in the early ‘60s if a drummer could play “Wipe Out” you know like okay you can be in our garage band. Was there something similar to that back then that you would be expected to be able to do?
